The black shaded region is located in the upper half of the large circle, and is the region remaining in the upper semicircle of the large circle after removing the upper halves of the two small circles. Reasoning: Each small circle has radius 1, and the two small circles are tangent at point O, so the distance from the center of each small circle to O is 1. The left and right endpoints A and C are respectively another 1 unit away from the corresponding small-circle center, therefore OA = OC = 2, and the radius of the large circle is 2. The area of the upper semicircle of the large circle is (1/2)π(2)^2 = 2π. The total area of the upper semicircles of the two small circles is 2 × (1/2)π(1)^2 = π. Therefore the shaded area is 2π - π = π. The area of one small circle is π(1)^2 = π, so the required ratio is π/π = 1.

From the text, each small circle has radius 1, their centers lie on AC, and they touch at O, the center of the large circle. Therefore each small-circle center is 1 unit from O, so A and C are 2 units from O; the large circle has radius 2. Compute the upper half of the large circle: (1/2)π(2)^2 = 2π.
